subject: Re: Astera v5b deploy - latency, errors, and throughput regression
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@astera.health>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: v5b deploy - latency spikes & 5xxs since midnight

Tessa —

We started seeing degraded page load times and an uptick in 5xx errors after your v5b rollout around 00:30 PDT. Key signals: p95 latency from 320ms -> 1.1s, overall error rate jumped from 0.2% to ~4.7%, and throughput for our hot endpoint dropped ~35%. This is on our production traffic (region: us-west).

Attached are a short sample of request traces and aggregated metrics for the past 6 hours (astera_error_log_0529.txt). Our customer success and engineering teams are blocked; we need an immediate mitigation plan. Can we get a rollback window or a hotfix?

Thanks,
Elena Park
Head of Platform
Astera Health

Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-29T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: v5b deploy - latency spikes & 5xxs since midnight

Tessa / team — investigating. Initial observations from our edge telemetry and runtime traces:

- The v5b-INT8 quant profile changed kernel selection patterns (FP32->INT8 path) for decoder attention. For a subset of long-context requests we are seeing KV-cache growth and decode stalls leading to p95 regression.
- There are also increased preemption/queueing events on a small pool of GPU hosts due to mixed precision kernel hot paths, causing transient 503s under sustained load.

Immediate mitigation options (ordered by risk/speed):
1) Hot rollback to v5a (previous variant) for Astera's production pool — fastest, low-risk. Requires routing change + model pin. Estimated lead time: 30–45 minutes to complete and validate.
2) Pin Astera to v5b-FP16 (a fallback variant with FP16 kernels) for their traffic split — medium effort, ~60–90 minutes.
3) Apply a temporary 'shorten-prefix' policy and KV-cache flush for affected routes to reduce KV growth — incremental but risky for output quality.

I'll attach the qprofile diff (qprofile-diff_v5a_v5b.txt) with kernel selection snippets and an excerpt from the trace showing the decode stall. I'm starting the rollback playbook as option 1 standby; please confirm if we should proceed.

-Karthik
Head of Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Elena Park <elena@astera.health>, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-29T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: v5b deploy - latency spikes & 5xxs since midnight

Hi Elena —

So sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as highest priority. Karthik's team recommends a rollback to v5a as the fastest way to restore baseline behavior. We'd like to schedule the rollback during the next 30–45 minutes (we can do a rapid canary first).

Proposed customer remediation: two weeks of usage credit for the impacted capacity and a joint post-mortem + tuning session where we'll walk through quant profile changes and a recommended testing checklist before future rollouts. If that works for you we'll initiate the rollback now.

Next steps (if you approve):
- 10:15 PDT: rapid canary to 5% traffic for 10 minutes, monitor p95 and 5xxs
- 10:30 PDT: full rollback to v5a for prod pool
- Post-rollback: 2-hour monitoring window and PM invite for 48 hours out

Apologies again — we'll keep you updated live.

Best,
Priyom Das
Commercial Lead — Health
Redwood Inference

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Park <elena@astera.health>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-30T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Update: rollback complete and monitors stable

Folks / Elena —

Quick update: we executed the rollback to v5a at 10:32 PDT yesterday per the plan. Runbook steps performed: variant pin + routing update, cache flush on the affected shard group, and a controlled mayfly canary before full cutover.

Observed results: p95 returned to baseline (~340ms) within 12 minutes of the full rollback; 5xx rate returned to <0.25% within 25 minutes. Throughput recovered to expected levels. I've attached the rollback checklist for your records (rollback_checklist.pdf).

Post-mortem plan: Karthik's team will produce a technical RCA focused on kernel selection and quant-match testing. We'll follow with a joint sync next week to review an expanded predeploy test matrix (including long-context KV pressure tests).

Priyom: I'll confirm the customer credit details and get an update on the PM invite.

Thanks for the quick collaboration — Elena, sorry again for the outage; we appreciate your patience.

Naomi Feldman
VP Sales — Enterprise Health
Redwood Inference
